transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Liam (Orion), Priya (Orion), Marcus (Orion)

Summary:
Quick Optimize product walkthrough focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), tradeoffs between quality and latency, and an initial plan to run a sandbox with Orion's prompts. Customer cares about sub-200ms median token latency for chat, and a 40-50% cost reduction target vs current hosted provider. Security/Private deployment questions surfaced (VPC, SOC2, KMS).

Topics:
- INT8 profiling and expected latency wins
- FP8 quality regressions and when to prefer FP8
- Caching, batching, and KV cache interplay with quantized models
- Dedicated vs Hosted for consistent p50/p90 latency
- Next steps: benchmark sheet, sandbox runs, data sharing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, today we're going to walk through Optimize and quantization profiles, Samira will drive the technical bits, uh Diego will chime in on the sandbox setup.
[00:15] Liam (Orion): hey thanks, yeah we're excited - our main thing is keeping latency tight for our chat product, we currently see about 220ms per token p50 on provider X and want to get under 180ms ideally.
[00:28] Samira (Redwood): cool, great context. quick preface — quantization is a knob, INT8 gives the best throughput gains usually but has more risk of small quality diffs; FP8 is, erm, a newer middle ground in some runtimes where you keep more fp dynamics and get a lot of latency/compute wins without as much quality drop.
[00:46] Priya (Orion): can you clarify, when you say INT8, is that post-training static quantization or some mixed precision approach? we currently run some 4-bit q with custom kernels.
[01:02] Samira (Redwood): good question — for Optimize we profile a model and create quantization profiles; we do per-layer calibration and often recommend per-workload INT8 with selective FP fallback on sensitive layers. that's basically static-like quant but with tuned calibration data. we also support FP8 where available on the hardware/kernel.
[01:25] Diego (Redwood): important to add — latency gains are both from smaller compute and memory bandwidth; INT8 on A100-ish hardware with our kernel selection can cut p50 token latency by ~30-50% in our benchmarks, FP8 sits around 20-35% depending on model and sequence length.
[01:45] Marcus (Orion): those are wide ranges — how do you surface the expected quality loss? do you do automatic evals?
[01:55] Samira (Redwood): yes, Optimize includes a quality vs latency matrix per profile. we run your sample prompt set and measure a set of metrics: perplexity-ish proxies, embedding cosine on reference outputs, and a small human eval sample for safety/critical flows. we show deltas in a dashboard so you can pick the profile.
[02:17] Liam (Orion): and the dashboard shows p50/p90 latency and cost estimates?
[02:22] Jordan (Redwood): yep; cost, token/sec, and latency distribution per profile. also we break down where gains come from — batching, kv/cache hits, lower kernel fp ops.
[02:33] Priya (Orion): what about caching? our workload is conversational with long contexts, KV cache hit rate is high - does that reduce the benefit of quantization?
[02:44] Samira (Redwood): caching helps reduce total work but quant still helps because the per-token decoder compute and memory reads are cheaper. for long contexts KV cache size is bigger, and on INT8 you sometimes see memory bus improvements which still help. there are cases, though, where for very high cache hit-rates the marginal latency improvement shrinks. we call that out in the profiler.
[03:10] Liam (Orion): security check — we will need to know about data residency and KMS — can you run Optimize on Private / VPC?
[03:18] Jordan (Redwood): yes, Private supports the same Optimize agent; we can either do sandbox in Hosted for speed or provision a Private sandbox if you need the network isolation. we have SOC2 docs and KMS integrations, you'll get audit logs.
[03:30] Marcus (Orion): any caveats around FP8 on different hardware vendors? we've seen one vendor with an fp8 path that's a bit shaky.
[03:39] Samira (Redwood): correct — kernel maturity varies. Optimize's profiler tags whether a profile uses vendor-specific FP8 kernels; we warn if fallback paths are needed. sometimes we recommend INT8 on that vendor until their FP8 path matures.
[03:58] Priya (Orion): our SLO is 200ms p50 and 350ms p90 for interactive chat. you mentioned p90 earlier — what are typical p90 regressions with INT8?
[04:10] Diego (Redwood): p90 can be impacted by tail events — variable seq lengths, cache misses, and cold starts. with dedicated capacity and steady batching policies p90 is predictable; INT8 itself doesn't usually increase p90 significantly if kernel selection and batching are tuned, but you can see larger variance in GPU-util spikes if batching isn't tuned.
[04:34] Liam (Orion): hmm okay. show us an example profile?
[04:38] Samira (Redwood): sure i'll talk through one — we profiled an Llama-3-ish 13B variant: baseline FP16 p50 ~ 180ms per token, INT8 ~120ms, FP8 ~135ms. quality delta measured by embedding cosine vs reference: INT8 -0.015 average, FP8 -0.006. human spot checks flagged a few hallucination regressions at INT8 on safety prompts.
[05:08] Marcus (Orion): so FP8 looks attractive — less quality hit and still decent latency. what's the expected cost delta?
[05:15] Jordan (Redwood): depends on throughput and batching; rough ballpark: INT8 can be 40-60% cheaper vs FP16 for token compute, FP8 around 30-45%. Optimize provides a cost-estimator tuned to your request mix.
[05:32] Liam (Orion): any known gotchas for function-calling structured outputs? we rely a lot on deterministic tokens.
[05:40] Samira (Redwood): structured outputs can be sensitive. we recommend running your function-calling prompts through both profiles and checking a determinism metric — we surface pass/fail for exact string match in the dashboard. if it fails, we suggest selective FP layers or keeping FP16 for that route.
[06:02] Priya (Orion): what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we want week-over-week results.
[06:08] Diego (Redwood): typical pilot: week 0 share prompts and performance targets, week 1 sandbox + initial runs, week 2 tuning & deeper evals, week 3 handoff/recommendations. we can compress if you give us more infra access or do hosted sandbox.
[06:25] Liam (Orion): what about dedicated vs hosted — our main ask is consistent p90 under load, is Dedicated required?
[06:33] Jordan (Redwood): Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and more consistent tail latency; for many customers with strict p90 SLOs Dedicated is recommended. but sometimes a hybrid approach: host initial pilot on Hosted with pinned model variants, then move to Dedicated for scale.
[06:49] Marcus (Orion): pricing curiosity — is Dedicated priced on commit or flat?
[06:53] Jordan (Redwood): it's reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; we'll share pricing.
[06:57] Liam (Orion): okay, any competitors we should watch out for?
[07:00] Samira (Redwood): folks often compare to OpenAI managed endpoints for simplicity, Anthropic for model behavior, and some infra shops use Replicate/self-hosted runtimes for cost control. we focus on a blend of operational controls, observability, and profiling.
[07:14] Priya (Orion): can you capture logs and link them to prompts? we need traceability for audit.
[07:20] Jordan (Redwood): yes, audit logs, per-token cost traces, and you can map tokens back to request ids — Private option gives extra retention/territory controls.
[07:28] Liam (Orion): any demo of the dashboard?
[07:30] Samira (Redwood): quick screen share — (screen noises) okay on the Optimize view, you can see a matrix: profiles across columns, metrics rows, and a per-prompt delta view; here sample row shows p50/p90, cost estimate, embedding delta, and a pass/fail column for deterministic routes.
[07:55] Samira (Redwood): note the profiler also surfaces which layers were sensitive and suggests per-layer FP fallback. that helped one customer keep INT8 throughput but keep safety-critical layers at FP16.
[08:10] Liam (Orion): nice — what's the granularity of the per-layer fallback? is it automatically applied at runtime or part of build time?
[08:18] Diego (Redwood): it's part of the build/deployment profile; Optimize creates a model variant with selective layers preserved in FP16/FP32 and the rest quantized. runtime supports automatic fallbacks for rare op incompatibilities, but per-layer choices are baked into the profile artifact.
[08:38] Marcus (Orion): we run some edge cases with long generated sequences, how do you measure quality there?
[08:45] Samira (Redwood): we do sequence-level metrics, and for long runs we sample final answers and check n-gram overlap, embedding similarity, and a small set of human labels for correctness. we flag divergence windows in the dashboard.
[09:02] Liam (Orion): okay this is helpful. what do you need from us to start?
[09:06] Jordan (Redwood): three things — 1) sample prompt set (1k), 2) your latency SLOs and traffic pattern, 3) permission for us to run sandbox workloads (hosted or private). once we have that we'll run Optimize and return a matrix and recommendations.
[09:22] Priya (Orion): we'll try to get the sample prompts by monday. one more question — do you handle model rollbacks automatically if quality regresses in prod?
[09:31] Samira (Redwood): yes, we support rollouts and can do canary tests with automatic rollback rules; Optimize ties into Rollouts.
[09:40] Marcus (Orion): good. any specific SOC/compliance docs we should look at?
[09:44] Jordan (Redwood): i'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and our security whitepaper; also include KMS integration guide.
[09:51] Liam (Orion): perfect.
[09:52] Jordan (Redwood): recap & next steps — Jordan will send benchmark spreadsheet and pricing by monday 2026-12-27; Samira/Diego will spin up a hosted sandbox with two quant profiles (INT8 and FP8) and run the 1k prompts once provided; Orion to share prompts and SLOs. schedule follow-up check-in in two weeks to review results.
[10:10] Priya (Orion): sounds good thanks everyone.
[10:12] Jordan (Redwood): thanks team, talk soon.
